correctness.rationale: The proof partitions ordered pairs of distinct 2-subsets into intersecting and disjoint orbit types, both transitive under A5. Every non-injective rank>=2 map f collapses one pair, yet permits a pair of each orbit type that is not collapsed; the disjoint case uses a fiber of size >=3 or a size-two fiber with two differing points in its complement. Thus a single f∘g distinguishes any prescribed ordered pair. The order 60 of A5 excludes 4-transitivity, which requires at least 120 ordered 4-tuples. Fresh independent enumeration of all 60 even permutations, 60 intersecting ordered pair configurations, 30 disjoint configurations, and all 3000 allowed maps (ranks 2:300,3:1500,4:1200) independently reproduced witnesses. This is exhaustive only because n=5 is fixed; the orbit proof supplies the group-theoretic reason.

originality.rationale: Hoffmann introduced strong sync-maximality and proved 4-transitive => strong => primitive while asking whether either inclusion is strict. His theorem does not imply that the natural A5 action is strongly sync-maximal; the candidate gives the missing lower strictness witness and an even stronger one-element property. Searches of semantic indexed findings and exact property/A5 literature returned no covering prior example. A prior unindexed observation remains possible.
